basis: The printing heads this block 'VERS. 16.' and it opens 'VERS. 16.-- Praecepitque ei dicens: Ex omni ligno paradisi comede, etc. Quaeritur quomodo'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Angelomus was a monk of Luxeuil in the middle of the ninth century and wrote for the Emperor Lothar I, who reigned from 840 to 855 and whom the verse prooemium addresses. The Genesis commentary is placed with his commentaries on Kings and on the Song of Songs in that decade. The wiki header gives the eleventh century, which is a century and a half out and is not followed. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1852 printing.
text: VERS. 16.-- Praecepitque ei dicens: Ex omni ligno paradisi comede, etc. Quaeritur quomodo loquebatur Adae Deus? Aut per coelestem substantiam, quomodo | nunc loquitur angelis; aut per corporalem speciem, id est ex aere coelesti sumpta imagine, sicut olim patriarchis; aut inspirando in mente, quomodo prophetis, sicut scriptum est: Dixit mihi, qui loquebatur in me? Sed sciendum est quia prius, antequam peccaret, loquebatur ei per coelestem substantiam, sicut angelis; postquam vero peccavit, per subjectam creaturam, id est per angelum.
